channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: Circuit Breaker Types Explained: MCB to OCB
item.description: What a circuit breaker does, the main types (MCB, MCCB, ACB, VCB, OCB, SF6, GIS), their parts, interrupting media, voltage-class selection and failure points.

item.title: Earth Fault Loop Impedance Explained: Why the Breaker Must Trip Fast Enough
item.description: What earth fault loop impedance is, the 0.4 s and 5 s disconnection times, how to find maximum Zs for MCB types, the 0.8 rule, maximum cable length and TT systems.

item.title: Motor Efficiency Classes Explained: IE1 to IE4, the EU Rules and What the Savings Look Like
item.description: What IE1 to IE4 motor efficiency classes mean under IEC 60034-30-1, the EU Ecodesign dates, a worked running cost comparison and why sizing and speed control matter too.

item.title: Motor Overload Protection: How Overload Relays and Trip Classes Work
item.description: How thermal overload relays protect motors, the IEC 60947-4-1 trip classes 10A, 10, 20 and 30 with trip times at 7.2 times setting, and how to match the class to the start.

item.title: Motor Starting Methods: DOL vs Star-Delta vs Soft Starter vs VFD Compared
item.description: Why starting current matters, how DOL, star-delta, soft starters and VFDs each tame it differently, and a comparison of current, torque, cost and complexity.

item.title: RCD, RCCB and RCBO Explained: How Residual Current Protection Works and Which Type to Use
item.description: How RCDs detect earth leakage, RCCB vs RCBO, the 30 mA rating and trip time limits, types AC, A, F and B, and how to select and test residual current devices.

item.title: What a Load Really Costs to Run
item.description: From nameplate kW to the electricity bill: load factor, efficiency, tiered tariffs, demand charges and marginal rate, with a worked motor example.

item.title: Types of Earthing Systems: 9 Electrode Types Explained
item.description: Nine types of earthing electrodes explained — plate, pipe, rod, strip, wire, chemical, ring, mesh and equipment earthing — what each is built from and used for.

item.title: VFD Speed Scaling: Why Affinity Laws Make Small Speed Cuts Deliver Outsized Savings
item.description: Motor speed scaling with VFD output frequency, and why the pump/fan affinity laws mean modest speed cuts trim power consumption by a much larger percentage.

item.title: Voltage Drop in LV Feeders: Why It's a Chain, Not a Single Number
item.description: Why voltage drop accumulates through every segment of a feeder chain, the formula behind it, and why a cable sized fine for ampacity can still fail on it.

item.title: Bearing Failures: Root Causes & Prevention
item.description: The five most common ways rolling-element bearings actually fail — spalling, lubrication breakdown, contamination, electrical erosion, and false brinelling.

item.title: Belt Drive Sizing: Why the Speed Ratio Alone Doesn't Tell You the Tension
item.description: Belt drive speed ratio, belt velocity and shaft torque from pulley diameters and power, and why tension depends on wrap angle and friction, not just geometry.

item.title: Compressed Air Systems: Where the Energy Goes and How to Cut It
item.description: Why compressed air is so expensive, how leaks and excess pressure waste energy, worked leak cost and pressure savings examples, receiver sizing and habits that cut cost.

item.title: Pipe Head Loss: Why Reynolds Number Decides Which Formula Applies
item.description: Pipe flow velocity, Reynolds number, friction factor and head loss.

item.title: Cavitation in Pumps: Causes, Warning Signs, and Prevention
item.description: What pump cavitation actually is, why NPSH available has to beat NPSH required, the field symptoms that give it away, and a practical prevention checklist.

item.title: Pump Power Explained: From Hydraulic Power to Shaft Power to Motor Size
item.description: How to get from flow and head to hydraulic power, shaft power and motor input, with a worked example, a standard motor size, and what density, speed and efficiency change.

item.title: Shaft Diameter Sizing: Combining Bending and Torsion with the ASME Equation
item.description: How the ASME shaft equation combines bending and torque with shock and fatigue factors, the allowable shear stress values, a worked 15 kW example and its limits.

item.title: Vibration Analysis Basics: ISO 20816-3 Severity Zones and What the Spectrum Tells You
item.description: How machine vibration is measured, the ISO 20816-3 severity zones by machine group, how alarms and change are set, and how unbalance, misalignment and bearing faults show in a spectrum.

item.title: Electrical Panel Factory Acceptance Test (FAT): The Complete Checklist
item.description: The 8 stages of an LV panel FAT — visual/mechanical inspection, insulation resistance, hi-pot, functional, protection and interlock tests, and documentation.

item.title: MCB, MCCB, ACB, RCCB & More: Electrical Switchgear & Protection Devices Explained
item.description: MCB, MCCB, ACB, VCB, SF6 breakers, RCCB, RCBO, ELCB, isolators, contactors, relays, fuses and busbars — what each device does and where it's used.

item.title: Piping Pressure Tests Explained: Hydrostatic and Pneumatic Leak Testing to ASME B31.3
item.description: How ASME B31.3 sets hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressures, the stress ratio correction, a worked example, hold time, and the practical hazards of static head, trapped air and stored energy.

item.title: Infrared Thermography for Electrical Inspection: Finding Hot Spots Before They Fail
item.description: How infrared surveys find loose and overloaded connections, the conditions that make a scan valid, the NETA temperature-difference criteria and a worked three-phase example.

item.title: Insulation Resistance Testing Explained
item.description: IEC 60364-6 / BS 7671 test voltages and minimums, motor spot IR and polarization index per IEEE 43, temperature correction and worked examples.

item.title: Pipe Wall Thickness (ASME B31.3)
item.description: ASME B31.3 pressure design thickness, corrosion allowance and the 12.5% mill tolerance, with a worked NPS 6 example and schedule selection.

item.title: Relief Valve Orifice Sizing
item.description: Set pressure, allowable overpressure, back pressure and relieving rate decide a relief valve's orifice area under API 520, and the scenario matters most.

item.title: Industrial Valves Explained: Types & Parts
item.description: What a valve does, the main types — gate, globe, ball, butterfly, check, plug, needle, diaphragm — its parts, a selection checklist, and common failure points.

item.title: Vessel Purging and Inerting Explained
item.description: Dilution purge turnovers, pressure-swing cycles and NFPA 69 oxygen targets, with worked examples for taking a vessel from air to a safe oxygen level.

item.title: Air Changes per Hour: What ACH Actually Tells You (and Doesn't)
item.description: What air changes per hour (ACH) measures, the formula behind it, typical ACH targets by space type.

item.title: Fan Static vs Total Pressure: What the Fan Is Really Working Against
item.description: How static, velocity and total pressure relate, how to work out fan total and static pressure from field readings, with worked examples for plenum and ducted inlets.

item.title: Heat Recovery Ventilation: HRV, ERV and What Effectiveness Really Means
item.description: How HRV and ERV units recover energy from exhaust air, the effectiveness formula, worked winter and summer examples, typical performance by type, and frost and leakage limits.
